chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim, from Salim ibn Mukram, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

My father said to Amr ibn Ubayd, Bashir al-Rahhal and Wasil in a narration: 'Neither drink from the ear (spout/handle) of the pitcher, nor from its crack if there is one in it — for it is a drinking place of the satans.'

key_terms.أُذُنُ الْكُوز: The 'ear' or handle/spout of the pitcher — the projecting part used to pour or hold the vessel
key_terms.كَسْر: A crack or break in the vessel
key_terms.مَشْرَبُ الشَّيَاطِينِ: The drinking place of the satans — the spiritual rationale for the prohibition

ai.seo_question: Is it forbidden to drink from the spout or crack of a pitcher in Islamic tradition?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) transmits a ruling from his father, Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (AS), who stated this to specific individuals in a narration. The prohibition against drinking from the spout or handle of a pitcher, or from a cracked vessel, is given a spiritual rationale: these openings are associated with the satans. This reflects the Shia jurisprudential tradition of grounding hygienic and behavioral norms in religious and spiritual reasoning.
